set.question: Which sentence makes a comparison?
options: Este acento es más fácil de entender que aquel. [This accent is easier to understand than that one.]
Mi familia usa este acento en las fiestas. [My family uses this accent at parties.]
Hablo con mi familia y con mis amigos hoy. [I speak with my family and my friends today.]

set.question: Which sentence expresses an opinion about language and identity?
options: Creo que la lengua influye en nuestra identidad. [I think language influences our identity.]
Hablo español en mi casa con mi familia. [I speak Spanish at home with my family.]
Mi lengua es española y la hablo en casa. [My language is Spanish and I speak it at home.]

set.question: Which sentence expresses contrast?
options: Aunque son diferentes, tienen algo en común. [Although they are different, they have something in common.]
Las dos tradiciones son muy parecidas entre sí. [The two traditions are very similar to each other.]
Esta fiesta es tan importante como la otra. [This celebration is as important as the other one.]

set.question: Which sentence expresses a sustained opinion?
options: Creo que las diferencias culturales pueden ser una oportunidad para aprender. [I think cultural differences can be an opportunity to learn.]
Las costumbres de cada región pasan de padres a hijos por muchos años. [The customs of each region pass from parents to children for many years.]
En cada comunidad hay diferencias de acento y de gramática entre las personas. [In each community there are differences of accent and grammar between people.]

set.question: Which sentence compares two things?
options: Esta variedad es más clara que la otra. [This variety is clearer than the other one.]
Esta variedad existe desde hace muchos años. [This variety has existed for many years.]
Hablo una lengua con mi familia en casa. [I speak a language with my family at home.]

set.question: Which statement best integrates the unit?
options: Las diferencias culturales pueden ser una oportunidad para aprender si escuchamos otras perspectivas. [Cultural differences can be an opportunity to learn if we listen to other perspectives.]
Las culturas de todo el mundo tienen normas sociales y tradiciones muy diferentes. [Cultures around the world have very different social norms and traditions.]
Hablo español con mi familia y con mis amigos después de vivir dos años en Budapest. [I speak Spanish with my family and friends after living two years in Budapest.]

set.question: Which statement best expresses balanced evaluation?
options: Una práctica puede ser diferente de la nuestra sin ser peor. [A practice can be different from ours without being worse.]
Una práctica diferente es peor que la nuestra. [A different practice is worse than ours.]
Todas las prácticas son iguales en las dos culturas. [All practices are the same in both cultures.]

old: "Use *más*...*que*, menos...que, *tan*...*como* and different descriptive structures to compare ways of speaking."
new: "You know *más … que*, *menos … que* and *tan … como* from A2 Unit 6. Use them to compare ways of speaking."

old: "*Tan* never changes for gender or number, even when the adjective next to it does: tan *interesante*, tan *interesantes* — only the adjective agrees, not *tan* itself."
new: "*Tan* never changes for gender or number; only the adjective agrees: *tan interesante*, *tan interesantes*."

old: "Explain how language can form part of identity and give opinions about its social importance."
new: "You know *creo que* and *pienso que* from B1 Unit 13. Use them to explain how language can be part of identity and to give opinions about its social importance."

old: "*Creo* *que* and *pienso* *que* take the indicative here because you're stating a belief, not doubting it — the subjunctive only shows up once you negate them (no *creo* *que*), a switch covered later in the course."
new: "*Creo que* and *pienso que* state a belief, so the verb stays in the indicative: *creo que influye*. Once you negate them, *no creo que* takes the subjunctive, as you saw in B1 Unit 13."

old: "Use es *importante* *que*, es *necesario* que and es *bueno* que with the subjunctive to evaluate cultural practices."
new: "You know *es importante que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. Use it, and *es necesario que* and *es bueno que*, to evaluate cultural practices."

old: "Notice that es *bueno* *que* works the same way as es *importante* *que* — any es + adjective + *que* construction that judges an action, rather than just reporting a fact, pulls the following verb into the subjunctive."
new: "*Es bueno que* works like *es importante que*: when you judge an action rather than report a fact, the next verb is in the present subjunctive."

old: "Compare cultures and practices with más...*que*, *menos*...que, tan...como, *pero*, *aunque* and sin embargo."
new: "You know *más … que*, *menos … que* and *tan … como* from A2 Unit 6, *aunque* and *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28. Use them with *pero* to compare cultures and practices."

old: "*Aunque* takes the indicative here (aunque *son* diferentes) because the difference is a known fact — save the subjunctive for *aunque* when what follows is hypothetical or not yet confirmed."
new: "*Aunque* takes the indicative when the difference is a known fact: *aunque son diferentes*. *Sin embargo* opens a new sentence: *Son diferentes. Sin embargo, tienen algo en común.*"

old: "Combine comparison, explanation, evaluation and opinion to discuss language, culture and identity."
new: "You know every structure here: comparison (A2 Unit 6), *creo que* (B1 Unit 13), *es importante que* + subjunctive (A2 Unit 27) and *aunque* (A2 Unit 28). Combine them to discuss language, culture and identity."

old: "Aunque nuestras costumbres son diferentes, creo que tan importante es escuchar como comparar."
new: "Aunque nuestras costumbres son diferentes, creo que escuchar es tan importante como comparar."

old: "A sustained discussion needs more than one structure per sentence: notice how the model answer stacks a comparison (*tan* importante *como*) inside a concession (*aunque*) instead of using them one at a time."
new: "A longer answer uses more than one structure: in the third example, *aunque* opens a concession and *tan importante como* gives the comparison."
